answer: Agents trading nectar in umber jars could bridge newcomers into a market through bonded sponsors. Each sponsor receives a fixed total credit limit shared across every agent it introduces; creating more aliases never expands that limit. A sponsor loses collateral when signed evidence proves an introduced agent double-spent. Attackers must obtain more bonded credit or risk their sponsors' funds. Colluding sponsors and wealthy attackers remain threats, and honest newcomers may struggle to find backing.
